explanation: Viroids and prions are sub-viral infectious particles. Viroids consist of naked strands of RNA with no surrounding capsid. They are associated with several crop diseases, instructing host plant cells to replicate more viroids. Prions, or proteinaceous infectious particles, are abnormal proteins. They share a similar primary sequence with normal cellular proteins but possess a different, contagious tertiary conformation. When prions interact with normal proteins, they force them to adopt the abnormal conformation at an exponential rate. Prions cause neurodegenerative diseases known as Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathies (TSEs). A notable example is Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE, or Mad Cow disease), which occurs in cattle and can be transmitted to humans.

questions.q: What is the structure of a viroid?
opts: An infectious protein with a modified tertiary shape
A naked strand of RNA with no capsid
A double-stranded DNA molecule inside a capsid
An enveloped RNA virus that infects animals
questions.exp: The notes define viroids as 'Naked strands of RNA – no capsid'.

questions.q: How do prions propagate inside a host organism?
opts: They transcribe their RNA genome into DNA using reverse transcriptase
They cause normal proteins in the host to change into the abnormal prion conformation at an exponential rate
They hijack host ribosomes to translate their genetic material
They multiply via binary fission within host tissues
questions.exp: Prions propagate by causing the conformation of normal proteins in the organism to convert into prions at an exponential rate.

questions.q: What class of diseases are prions associated with?
opts: Plant crop blight and mosaic diseases
questions.exp: Prions are associated with neurodegenerative diseases, or Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathies (TSEs), such as Mad Cow disease.
